questiontext.text:
A boda boda wheel is made up of a metal rim with a rubber tyre fitted around it. The rim has a radius of \({@r@}\,\text{cm}\), and the tyre extends a further \({@Thickness@}\,\text{cm}\) beyond the rim, giving an outer radius of \({@R@}\,\text{cm}\).

Calculate the area of the rubber cross-section (the shaded ring shown), correct to \(2\,\text{decimal places}\). (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\))

[[jsxgraph]] var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-9, 9, 9, -9], axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Fixed DISPLAY radii, independent of the true R and r (which are in cm) var R_outer = 6; var R_inner = 3.5; // Centre of the wheel, labelled clearly, offset AWAY from the radius lines var O = brd.create('point', [0, 0], { name: 'O', visible: true, size: 3, strokeColor: 'red', fillColor: 'red', fixed: true, label: { offset: [-8, 14], fontSize: 16, color: 'red' } }); // Outer circle drawn FIRST, filled dark grey/black to represent the rubber tyre var tyre = brd.create('circle', [O, R_outer], { strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: 'black', fillColor: '#2b2b2b', fillOpacity: 1 }); // Inner circle drawn ON TOP, filled light silver to represent the metal rim // This "cuts out" the centre, leaving only the dark ring (the tyre) shaded var rim = brd.create('circle', [O, R_inner], { strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: 'black', fillColor: '#d9d9d9', fillOpacity: 1 }); // Two radius lines drawn at well-separated angles so labels never overlap var angleRim = 100 * Math.PI / 180; // pointing up-left, inside the rim var angleTyre = -40 * Math.PI / 180; // pointing down-right, into the tyre var P_rim = brd.create('point', [ R_inner * Math.cos(angleRim), R_inner * Math.sin(angleRim) ], {size: 0, fixed: true, visible: false}); var P_tyre = brd.create('point', [ R_outer * Math.cos(angleTyre), R_outer * Math.sin(angleTyre) ], {size: 0, fixed: true, visible: false}); // Rim radius line: bright yellow, high contrast against the grey rim fill brd.create('segment', [O, P_rim], {strokeColor: '#ffcc00', strokeWidth: 3, dash: 2}); // Tyre (outer) radius line: bright cyan, high contrast against the black tyre fill brd.create('segment', [O, P_tyre], {strokeColor: '#00e0ff', strokeWidth: 3, dash: 2}); // Rim radius label, placed clearly along its own line, away from O's label brd.create('text', [ R_inner * 0.55 * Math.cos(angleRim) - 1.4, R_inner * 0.55 * Math.sin(angleRim) + 0.6, function() { return {#r#} + ' cm'; } ], { fontSize: 14, color: '#b8860b' }); // Outer (tyre) radius label, placed along its own line, in open space brd.create('text', [ R_outer * 0.62 * Math.cos(angleTyre) + 0.3, R_outer * 0.62 * Math.sin(angleTyre) - 0.6, function() { return {#R#} + ' cm'; } ], { fontSize: 14, color: '#008fb3' }); // Simple legend so students can instantly tell rim from tyre brd.create('text', [-8.5, -7, 'Grey = Rim'], { fontSize: 13, color: '#555555' }); brd.create('text', [-8.5, -7.8, 'Black = Rubber tyre'], { fontSize: 13, color: '#2b2b2b' }); [[/jsxgraph]]

\(\text{Area of rubber cross-section}=\)[[input:ans1]]\(\,\text{cm}^2\)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

The rubber cross-section of the tyre forms an annulus — a ring-shaped region between the outer edge of the tyre and the metal rim. From the problem:

  • Rim radius (inner): \(r={@r@}\,\text{cm}\)
  • Tyre thickness: \({@Thickness@}\,\text{cm}\)

Step 1: Find the outer radius \(R\).

\( \begin{align} R &= r + \text{Thickness} \\ &= {@r@} + {@Thickness@} \\ &= {@R@}\,\text{cm} \end{align} \)

Step 2: Write the formula for the area of an annulus.

\[ A = \pi (R^2 - r^2) \]

Step 3: Substitute the values and compute the area.

\( \begin{align} A &= \frac{22}{7} \times \left({@R@}^2 - {@r@}^2\right) \\ &= \frac{22}{7} \times \left({@R_sq@} - {@r_sq@}\right) \\ &= \frac{22}{7} \times {@Radius_difference@} \\ &= {@A@}\,\text{cm}^2 \end{align} \)

Rounded to \(2\) decimal places:

\(\text{Area of rubber cross-section} \approx {@A_2dp@}\,\text{cm}^2\)
